Report Description/// CORRECTION TO REPORT # 1429713 /// POTENTIAL RELEASE /// CORRECTED INFORMATION IS AS FOLLOWS: -THE INCIDENT CAUSE CHANGED FROM BOMB THREAT TO OTHER. /// CRITICAL INCIDENT COMMUNICATIONS (CIC) REPORT - INITIAL/FINAL - UNEXPLODED ORDNANCE IN WATERWAY CAPE MAY, NJ - 28 APRIL 2025 /// AMPLIFYING INFORMATION: • AT 1610 EASTERN, A BEACHGOER AT HIGBEE BEACH IN CAPE MAY, NJ LOCATED UNEXPLODED ORDNANCE. • CAPE MAY COUNTY BOMB SQUAD WAS NOTIFIED. BY THE TIME THEY ARRIVED AT THE SCENE, THE TIDE HAD COME IN AND WASHED THE ORDNANCE BACK OUT TO SEA. • THE ORDNANCE IS BELIEVED TO BE IN THE PATH OF THE INCOMING CAPE MAY FERRY, MOTOR VESSEL (M/V) DELAWARE, WHICH HAS BEEN TURNED AROUND DUE TO CONCERNS THAT THE PROP WASH COULD JOSTLE THE ORDNANCE AND CAUSE IT TO EXPLODE. THE PASSENGERS ON THE FERRY ARE DISGRUNTLED WITH THE VESSEL BEING TURNED AROUND TO LEWES, DELAWARE. • THE CAPE MAY-LEWES FERRY CAN CARRY APPROXIMATELY 800 PASSENGERS AND 100 VEHICLES PER CROSSING. • THERE WAS DREDGING IN THE AREA WHICH HAS BEEN HALTED UNTIL DEEMED SAFE TO RESUME. • THE ONLY OTHER TRAFFIC IN THE AREA IS SMALL RECREATIONAL VESSELS WHICH DO NOT POSE A RISK OF DISTURBING THE BOTTOM OF THE CHANNEL. • THE EXPLOSIVE ORDNANCE DISPOSAL UNITS AT NAVAL WEAPONS STATION EARLE AND NAVAL WEAPONS STATIONS YORKTOWN HAVE BEEN CONSULTED AND AGREE THAT EVEN THOUGH THE DETONATION HEAD OF THE ORDNANCE COULD NOT BE SEEN, IT STILL MAY BE CAPABLE OF EXPLODING. • LOCAL LAW ENFORCEMENT IS NO LONGER INVOLVED. THEY WILL BE NOTIFIED IF THE ORDNANCE WASHES BACK ON SHORE. • USCG STATION CAPE MAY WILL BE CONDUCTING A HARBOR PATROL AND BEACH WALK AT FIRST LIGHT TO SEE IF THE ORDNANCE RESURFACES. • USCG SECTOR DELAWARE BAY PUBLIC AFFAIRS WILL BE RELEASING A STATEMENT IN TANDEM WITH THE USCG DISTRICT FIVE PUBLIC AFFAIRS OFFICER. • THE CIC PROCESS WAS STOOD DOWN WITH CONCURRENCE FROM BOTH AREAS. CASE PENDS.
